prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and the development of long-acting incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: The round-1 exchange has confirmed that B023 is the one configuration all six of us hold, and that the open questions are attribution and citation wording, not merit or maturity. The chain from proglucagon and incretin physiology (Holst, Drucker) to acylated, albumin-binding analogues (Knudsen) and then to independently replicated outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease is complete and stable. Delay has a real cost because the laureates are living. A three-person prize naming two physiologists and the scientist who solved the half-life problem states clearly why patients benefit, which is the test the will sets. I therefore keep Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, with a citation that names both the physiology and the long-acting therapies.
statement.case_against: No three names from this ballot are fully fair. Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is a real claim, Habener and Bell sit outside the credited names, and I cannot settle the priority question from the supplied record. Knudsen's seat also means a company-based scientist stands for a long industrial programme, and the prize can be read as a compound of academic physiology and drug development. I considered a second part, but any pairing with B051 or B001 would add at least two further people and break the three-person cap. A split of B023 into two parts would force the same names into both parts without a distinct achievement. A single, clearly worded part is the more defensible choice.

responses.point: Perlmann keeps Mojsov in the third seat and holds the citation to the physiology and the active peptide, arguing that identification of the active peptide is upstream of every analogue.
responses.response: I take the upstream argument seriously, but it does not settle the choice, because you also state that Mojsov's priority is contested and that Habener and Bell belong to the same story. A seat built on a claim we cannot adjudicate is more fragile than one built on the design of liraglutide and semaglutide, which nobody disputes. I also do not accept that Knudsen's work is optimisation. Making a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly drug was a protein-chemistry and pharmacology problem, and the citation wording I propose still names the physiology, so your concern that the prize stay tied to discovery is met in the text. If the committee cannot name the peptide-identification credit with confidence, I would rather say so in the citation by crediting the physiology broadly than rest a seat on an unresolved priority.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved Knudsen into his trio in place of Mojsov after rereading colleagues' ballots, and ranks the unfolded protein response as the strongest alternative while noting that its disease relevance is partly correlative.
responses.response: I welcome that move, and I note that you reached it by weighing the contested priority against an undisputed drug-design step, which is the reasoning I rely on. On B051 I accept your caveat that clean two-person attribution must not stand in for merit, and that Ron's PERK and integrated stress response work is outside the credited names. That is why B051 stays an alternative and not a second part. It is also why I would not pair it with B023 this year. It would bring two more names, exceed the cap, and add the achievement with the least direct clinical consequence. I would keep B051 first among alternatives for the case where GLP-1 attribution collapses.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius holds that the prize-worthy core is the combination of target discovery and drug design, and adds that long-term safety of the incretin class beyond weight and glucose is still being defined.
responses.response: Your view that the core is the combination answers the chair's question about citation wording, and I adopt it: the citation should name both the physiology and the long-acting therapies. On safety, I agree that effects beyond weight and glucose are still being characterised, and that is the reason to keep the citation to the established indications, type 2 diabetes and obesity, and not to list the cardiovascular and renal benefits as the achievement. I do not think the open safety questions weigh against maturity, because a decade of independent trials has defined the benefit-risk profile of the class well enough for recognition, and the Nobel record includes therapies whose later safety work continued after the prize.

responses.point: El Manira ranks CAR-T above the unfolded protein response and cGAS-STING because it has direct, durable benefit in refractory leukaemia and lymphoma, while accepting that Eshhar is not credited.
responses.response: I agree that CAR-T has the strongest clinical evidence among the alternatives and your point on ordering is fair. I ranked it fourth for the same reason you describe: durable remissions, with the weakness that Eshhar's chimeric receptor work is outside the credited names and that a three-name credit for June, Sadelain and Rosenberg compresses a multi-group history. I still keep B051 and B001 as my listed alternatives, because they have the cleaner conceptual claims. If the committee decides that clinical benefit must carry more weight in a fallback, I would accept B022 ahead of them, but I would not use it to expand this year's configuration to two parts.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide should displace Knudsen, which I cannot resolve from the supplied record, and how Habener and Bell should be treated.
Whether the committee accepts a company-based development scientist alongside two academic discoverers as a defensible compound achievement.
Whether the support for B023 across all six members reflects the obviousness of impact more than a settled allocation of credit.
Whether the exact division of early unfolded protein response credit between Mori and Walter, recalled by Linnarsson from memory, would hold up if B051 became the fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My Greengard postdoctoral period and roughly twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann are documented, though neither the count nor the works concern any shortlisted candidate, so I propose no recusal. As chair I have tried to treat my own round-1 position as one voice and not as the committee's. I note my neurology background only as context and not as a preference for any candidate.
